title: Bitopological Manifolds: Properties and Examples
content: We introduce and investigate a differential-topological framework for manifolds equipped with two interacting topologies. A bitopological manifold is defined as a set endowed with two manifold topologies together with compatible smooth structures. The two topologies are allowed to be different, and consequently one obtains two notions of convergence, closure, interior, compactness, continuity, and smoothness. We formulate the notions of pairwise continuity, pairwise smoothness, bitopological charts, bitopological atlases, pairwise Hausdorffness, pairwise compactness, and pairwise connectedness. We establish basic properties of these structures and describe conditions under which the two topologies coincide. Several examples are given, including the diagonal case of an ordinary smooth manifold, manifolds arising from two diffeomorphic but distinct topologies, product constructions, and bitopological manifolds associated with ordered manifolds. The framework is motivated by the classical theory of bitopological spaces initiated by Kelly and developed subsequently through pairwise separation, quasi-uniformity, covering properties, and related constructions. The purpose of the present paper is to transfer these ideas to a differential-geometric setting and to provide a convenient language for future studies of geometry on spaces carrying two compatible topological structures.
